title: Specs Supplemental Sidecar Schema
description: What a component needs beyond what the spec can carry, authored beside it as supplemental.yaml. The audience is whoever builds the component. Overlay-only: every entry names the schema path that cannot carry it, so anything the schema can carry belongs in the spec. What a component's user must observe is the other sidecar's subject — guidelines.schema.json. Three scopes share this shape: one component, every component, and one foundation; entries across scopes are additive rather than overriding (DSPEC-56). (ADR-118)

anatomy.description: Requirements about the element tree: what parts a component has and how they nest.

props.description: Requirements about the props a component takes, and what a caller may pass.

styles.description: Requirements about the style values a component's parts carry.

slotComposition.description: Requirements about what may fill a slot, in what quantity, and in what arrangement.

events.description: Requirements about what a component emits, and when.

accessibility.description: Requirements about what assistive technology receives, and what a caller must supply for it.

behavior.description: Requirements about what a component does in response to interaction or state.

motion.description: Requirements about how a component traverses a change rather than where it ends up.

layout.description: Requirements about how a component's parts are arranged and sized relative to each other.

overrides.description: Requirements about what a caller may replace or supply in place of a component's own part.

naming.description: Requirements about why a component, prop, or part carries the name it does.

Section.description: Entries for one concern the spec cannot fully carry.

SchemaGap.description: The surface that would carry a requirement, and why it cannot. Named rather than asserted — an entry that cannot name its gap belongs in the spec.

path.description: The schema pointer or workspace-relative target that would carry this. A JSON Schema pointer is resolved by a validator (DSPEC-58); a gap in the library's own data names the report instead, because a missing motion token is not a gap in styles.schema.json.

need.description: What that target cannot express, and why it cannot.

SupplementalEntry.description: One requirement the spec cannot carry.

intent.description: A testable statement of what the component must do, written to transfer directly to a test criterion. No rationale prose.

schemaGap.description: The surface that would carry this requirement, and why it does not.

platforms.description: The platforms this applies to. Absent means every platform.

checks.description: What does the checking. Required when checkedBy is automated.
